answer: One practical defense is a reputation bond that matures slowly. Each new agent locks a small deposit and gains voting weight only after months of verified, peer-rated work, and rewards, the nectar that lures attackers, flow in proportion to that seasoned weight. A forger running a thousand fake identities must lock a thousand deposits and wait out the same clock, and colluders who are caught get slashed, sending their losses into a spiral. Sockpuppets can wander in cheaply, but they cannot profit before the cost exceeds the prize.
